items.claim: The row's back boundary (Song.8.5|8.6) is asserted without any tier-1 marker, and its rejected alternative is a strawman that never engages the strongest real rival: extending the unit forward into 8:6, since the 1cs-speaker/2ms-addressee pattern established in 8:5's second half continues unbroken across the cut.
items.evidence: 8:5b already shifts internally from 3fs description ('al dodah, 'upon her beloved') to a 1cs speaker addressing a 2ms 'you' -- תַּ֤חַת הַתַּפּ֨וּחַ֙ עֽוֹרַרְתִּ֔יךָ 'under the apple tree I awakened you' (oshb:Song.8.5, byte tier), 2ms suffix marking the addressee. That exact 1cs/2ms pattern persists with no intervening marker into 8:6's opening imperative, שִׂימֵ֨נִי כַֽחוֹתָ֜ם עַל לִבֶּ֗ךָ 'set me as a seal upon your heart' (oshb:Song.8.6, byte tier), again a 2ms suffix. The row discloses the internal 8:5a/8:5b shift honestly but never discloses this cross-seam continuity into 8:6, and its rejected_alternative compares only against a whole-verse plain lyric_address, never against the stronger candidate of folding 8:5's address half into the 8:6-7 epigram it grammatically matches.

items.claim: The row states no tier-1 warrant for its own front boundary (Song.8.5|8.6) -- the same 1cs/2ms address pattern from 8:5b runs unbroken into 8:6, an undisclosed cross-seam continuity device -- and its second Hebrew quote/gloss pair inserts an English 'for' translating a word that falls outside the quoted span.
items.evidence: boundary_evidence_refs cites only the self-span and the 8:7 setumah; no marker is offered for why 8:6 opens a new unit rather than continuing 8:5b's 1cs-to-2ms address (עֽוֹרַרְתִּ֔יךָ 'I awakened you' into שִׂימֵ֨נִי כַֽחוֹתָ֜ם עַל לִבֶּ֗ךָ 'set me as a seal upon your heart', oshb:Song.8.5-Song.8.6, byte tier, same 2ms suffix). Separately, the row quotes the strong-as-death clause as 'for love is strong as death', but the full available clause is כִּֽי עַזָּ֤ה כַמָּ֨וֶת֙ אַהֲבָ֔ה (oshb:Song.8.6, byte tier) -- the opening particle 'ki' ('for/because') sits immediately before the row's cited span and is excluded from it, yet 'for' appears in the attached gloss: a quote/gloss same-span violation.

items.claim: The row's front boundary is carried by a genuine in-verse person-marked pivot, and the achot role-split against the achoti bride-epithet inventory is byte-accurate.
items.evidence: 8:8 opens on the 1cp possessive אָח֥וֹת לָ֨נוּ֙ 'a little sister [belongs] to us' (oshb:Song.8.8, byte tier), a clean shift from the 1cs woman's voice running through 8:6-7 to a new plural speaker-group (the brothers) -- a legitimate morphological voice-shift marker, not continuity-inferred. The achot token here is correctly role-split from the achoti bride-epithet zone (4:9-5:2, cited in boundary_evidence_refs as web:Song.4.9-Song.5.2) per the book's own achot/achoti hazard; the back boundary at 8:9|8:10 is independently carried by the 1cs ani pivot argued in the neighboring row. epigram_unit is a defensible operative-category application (a short self-contained deliberative mashal), and the rejected dialogue_exchange alternative is reasonable since the strategy's own named dialogue_exchange zones do not include this span.

items.claim: The ani chomah pronoun pivot is an unambiguous tier-1 marker for the front boundary, and the petuchah is correctly disclosed as tier-3 corroboration only, not the driver.
items.evidence: 8:10 opens אֲנִ֣י חוֹמָ֔ה 'I am a wall' (oshb:Song.8.10, byte tier), an explicit 1cs pronoun return from the brothers' 1cp voice in 8:8-9 -- a clean, unambiguous morphological marker. The petuchah citation (oshb:Song.8.10 (petuchah, single-witness)) is named as accompanying structural coincidence, not as the seam driver, matching the single PE against nineteen SAMEKH in the 20-mark inventory (sweep: 1 of 20 marked verses); confidence is calibrated slightly above its medium_low siblings for a stated reason (a crisper tier-1 marker than the neighboring rows), not left at an unexamined level.

items.claim: The row's boundary_rationale and boundary_evidence_refs name only the tier-3 petuchah at 8:10 as the stated front-seam evidence; the actual tier-1 warrant (the person shift from her 1cs declaration into 3ms narration naming Solomon) is disclosed only inside strongest_rejected_alternative rather than being named as the driver where seam warrant is expected.
items.evidence: boundary_rationale's only explicit seam citation is 'the immediately preceding verse (web:Song.8.10) carries the book's petuchah division' -- tier-3 corroboration that must never be a boundary driver. The real grammatical pivot, 8:10's 1cs אֲנִ֣י חוֹמָ֔ה giving way to 8:11's 3ms narrative naming לִשְׁלֹמֹה֙ 'to Solomon' (oshb:Song.8.11, byte tier), is only named in strongest_rejected_alternative ('the shift to third-person Solomon narration'), leaving the row's primary seam-warrant field resting on a tier-3 mark alone.

items.claim: The Hebrew quote excludes 'chaverim' ('companions'), yet the attached English gloss translates that omitted word -- a quote/gloss same-span violation.
items.evidence: The row quotes the listening-clause as 'companions listening for your voice, let me hear it', but the quoted Hebrew span it cites begins at the participle 'listening' -- the full available clause in the verse is חֲבֵרִ֛ים מַקְשִׁיבִ֥ים לְקוֹלֵ֖ךְ הַשְׁמִיעִֽינִי (oshb:Song.8.13, byte tier), where 'chaverim' ('companions') precedes the row's quoted span and is not part of it. 'Companions' nonetheless appears unbracketed in the gloss, translating a word outside the cited byte span.
